audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge is named as matchup-defining in eleven separate full-layer strings — "Track Satchel Charge before every commit", "Engage only on Satchel Charge's cooldown", "Commit on Satchel Charge's cooldown" — and its cooldown is never once stated.
audit.why: The entire matchup plan is organised around waiting out one ability, and the reader is never told how long the wait is. It is 20/18/16/14/12. At rank 1 that is 20 seconds against Nasus's own Wither at 15 — his disengage is longer than your engage tool, which is precisely the mechanical reason the full layer's phrase "Wither wins the rematch" is true. Stating both numbers turns a slogan into a plan.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 against Wither's 15s — your slow comes back first, which is why the rematch is yours.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield is treated purely as a wall of damage to be feared — "don't facecheck the mines on your approach" — with no mention of its damage falloff.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage." For Nasus this is decision-changing rather than trivia. He has no dash and no way around the minefield; his only route to Ziggs is straight through it. Knowing that he eats one mine at full value and diminishing ones after turns an approach that looks suicidal into one that is routinely correct. The current advice tells him to avoid the one thing he must walk through.
audit.corrected: Successive detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, so walking the minefield costs one real mine and diminishing ones after — go through it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Short Fuse is never mentioned in either layer, and the early-game text implies Ziggs is harmless once you are close.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Periodically, Ziggs' next basic attack deals bonus magic damage. This cooldown is reduced whenever Ziggs uses an ability." Ziggs is a mage who poked constantly, which means Short Fuse is coming off cooldown fast, and the empowered auto lands on whatever is next to him — which in this matchup is Nasus. The guide's picture of a purely ranged poke champion misses a recurring chunk of magic damage in the exact phase it tells Nasus to walk in.
audit.corrected: Short Fuse periodically empowers his basic attack, and every ability he casts brings it back sooner — he is not harmless at melee range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge's delayed detonation is not mentioned; it is described only as a knockback.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Ziggs flings an explosive charge that detonates after a delay, or when this ability is activated again." There is a window between the charge landing and it going off, which is the counterplay — you can step out of the blast during the delay rather than simply accepting the knockback. The self-knockback ("Ziggs is also knocked away, but takes no damage") is correctly captured in the full layer as "self-peel escape", which is right and I left it.
audit.corrected: Satchel Charge detonates on a delay or on re-activation — you can walk out of the blast rather than eat the knockback.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Inferno Bomb is described as generic zone control with no range and no falloff.
audit.why: It reaches 5000 units and "enemies in the primary blast zone take more damage than those farther away". The range explains why the late-game section is right that he zones objectives from somewhere Nasus cannot contest, and the falloff is actionable: if the bomb is already committed, being off-centre meaningfully reduces what it does. Cooldown is 120/95/70.
audit.corrected: Mega Inferno Bomb reaches 5000 units and hits hardest at the centre — if it is landing on you, do not be in the middle of it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Item and rune advice is matchup-specific here rather than templated: report[8].t recommends Spirit Visage and Mercury's Treads, and wants.you[2] says buy early MR.
audit.why: That is the right call against an all-magic-damage kit and is notably better than the generic Frozen Heart / Plated Steelcaps block that appears in the other Nasus entries I audited. Left unchanged.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ziggs.json — all abilities deal magic damage

audit.whatIsWrong: The _missing-interactions file asserts "Ziggs bypasses stacking resistances (Satchel Charge (W)) — raw armour or MR is the wrong answer here." I do not believe this is true of Satchel Charge against champions.
audit.why: Riot's description of Satchel Charge says only "The explosion deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away" — no percent-health component. The kit file's percentHealth flag on W appears to be derived from the turret clause, "Ziggs can use the Satchel to hexplode vulnerable enemy turrets", which is structure damage and irrelevant to a Nasus health bar. I have therefore written nothing into the matchup on this basis, and flagged it rather than propagate it.
audit.corrected: Treat the percentHealth flag on Ziggs W as a probable false positive from the turret text; MR is a valid answer in this matchup.

edits.after: Hexplosive Minefield zones your stacking, but successive mines on the same target deal reduced damage — walk it.

edits.before: Fury of the Sands gives you bulk and a possible all-in, but his R + Satchel disengage keep the lane a coinflip.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands gives you bulk and an all-in, but Satchel Charge is a 20s reset on any commit you make.

edits.before: Ziggs owns the first two levels outright — his Q bounce-bomb out-ranges every tool you have, so don't try to walk up and trade, just soak XP and last-hit with Spirit Fire (E) from max range where his bombs can't punish you for stepping into the wave. Your Soul Eater lifesteal means his individual Q pokes don't actually threaten you the way they would a squishy; you out-sustain a single bomb if you don't get greedy. At 3 Wither flips the script for the first time — if he ever steps up to shove or you can flank, slap the slow on him and he physically cannot kite your autos.
edits.after: Ziggs owns the first two levels outright — Bouncing Bomb out-ranges every tool you have at 850 and is only a 6s cooldown at rank 1, so don't walk up to trade. Soak XP and last-hit with Spirit Fire (E) from max range. Soul Eater lifesteal means single bombs don't threaten you the way they would a squishy. Watch Short Fuse though: his passive periodically empowers a basic attack and every ability he casts brings it back sooner, so he is not harmless up close. At 3 Wither flips the script and he cannot kite your autos.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are a patience game: he's poking with Q and zoning your stack-farm with the E minefield, so weave E for last-hits and don't facecheck the mines on your approach. Your only kill pressure is Wither — once it's down he loses the move speed to escape, and his only answer is Satchel (W) to knock you off. Bait that W: walk in like you're committing, let him blow it, then re-engage with Wither when his one disengage tool is on cooldown. His R is just zone control here, not a duel threat to your fat HP bar.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are a patience game: he pokes with Bouncing Bomb and zones your stack-farm with Hexplosive Minefield. Don't fear the minefield — successive detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, so you eat one real mine and diminishing ones walking through it. Your only kill pressure is Wither: once he is slowed he loses the move speed to escape, and his answer is Satchel Charge, 20s at rank 1. Bait it, let him blow it, then re-engage while his one disengage tool is down.

edits.before: Once you have Sheen/Iceborn and stacks, the straight all-in is yours — Wither plus an empowered Q burst kills a squishy Ziggs the moment you get on top of him past his Satchel. But this lane never fully becomes a stomp: Ziggs is a siege/poke specialist, so on the map he zones you off objectives with R and a stacked minefield from a range you can't contest. Force your all-ins when his W is down, look to flank him in skirmishes where he can't kite, and let your team punish him whenever he over-extends to siege.
edits.after: Once you have Sheen/Iceborn and stacks, the straight all-in is yours — Wither plus an empowered Q kills a squishy Ziggs the moment you get on top of him past Satchel Charge. But this never becomes a stomp: Mega Inferno Bomb is hurled 5000 units, so he zones objectives from a range you cannot contest. Its outer edge does less than the centre, so if it is landing on you, do not be in the middle. Force all-ins when his W is down and flank him where he cannot kite.

notes: The clearest gap here was structural rather than factual: the full layer names Satchel Charge as the thing to track in eleven separate strings and never states its cooldown once. Supplying it (20s at rank 1) also supplies the reason the layer's own slogan 'Wither wins the rematch' is true, since Wither is 15s and comes back first. The most useful correction is on Hexplosive Minefield — successive detonations on the same target deal reduced damage, which matters enormously for a champion with no dash whose only route to Ziggs is straight through the mines, and the existing text told him to avoid exactly that. IMPORTANT: I deliberately did not use the _missing-interactions entry claiming Satchel Charge bypasses stacking resistances. Riot's description gives it no percent-health component against champions, and the percentHealth flag looks derived from the turret-hexplode clause. If other agents are working from that file unfiltered, that headline is likely to get written into several Ziggs matchups as fact — worth checking. Note also that report[8].t here correctly carries a magic-resist build (Spirit Visage, Mercury's Treads) rather than the templated armour block seen in the other Nasus entries.
